title: Webhook delivery
summary: From a change in the platform to a signed POST at an application's endpoint. The journal append is part of the change itself; everything after it happens in a separate worker. The top row is how a webhook or a delivery is stopped, and the right side is the retry loop.

boxes.label: Domain change
boxes.detail: Three writers: a workflow alert that activates, clears or is acknowledged; a geofence that is entered or exited, or a wandering rule that starts or resolves; and an automation's event action. Device connectivity alerts are not in this journal.

boxes.label: Journal append
boxes.detail: The writer must already be inside the transaction that makes the change. It locks the organization's stream row, inserts an integration-event.v1 row with the next sequence and a snapshot of the data, and writes each alert change once.

boxes.label: Webhooks worker
boxes.sub: Each second, 50 webhooks at a time
boxes.detail: Its own container running integrations:webhooks-work. For each enabled webhook it finishes the oldest pending delivery first; otherwise it takes the next journal event after the webhook's cursor whose device is in the application's grant. There is no choice of event types: an application has one webhook and receives every event for its granted devices.

boxes.label: Delivery row
boxes.detail: One row for each webhook and event, created with the exact body, the endpoint revision, an allowance of 5 attempts and a deadline of 24 hours. It is saved before any network call, so a crash retries the same delivery with the same ID. A pending delivery holds back newer events for that endpoint.

boxes.label: Check again
boxes.detail: Under a lock on the application: the webhook is still enabled, the delivery belongs to the current endpoint revision, the event's device is still granted, the deadline has not passed and the retry time has come. The destination must still be an approved HTTPS host on port 443 that resolves only to public IPv4 addresses.

boxes.label: Sign and send
boxes.sub: HMAC-SHA256, 3 s connect, 5 s in all
boxes.detail: Headers X-Iot-Delivery-Id, X-Iot-Timestamp and X-Iot-Signature: v1=<hex>. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp, a dot, the delivery ID, a dot and the raw body, keyed with the webhook's secret. The request goes to the address that was just validated, follows no redirect and uses no proxy. Each attempt is recorded, and an endpoint gets at most one send a second.

boxes.label: Receiver
boxes.detail: It must recompute the signature over the raw bytes before parsing, reject a timestamp more than 300 seconds off, and remember delivery or event IDs, because a retry repeats the ID with a new timestamp and a valid request can be replayed. The SDK's verifyWebhook does the first two.

boxes.label: Delivered
boxes.detail: The delivery is marked delivered and the worker moves on to the next event for this endpoint.

boxes.label: Failed
boxes.detail: Reached after the fifth attempt, when the 24 hours pass, or at once for any other response, a redirect included. The webhook stays enabled and newer events flow again. A manager can retry a failed delivery from the portal while it belongs to the current endpoint: it becomes pending with 5 more attempts and a new deadline.

boxes.label: Webhook disabled
boxes.detail: Happens when the application is revoked, its grant changes (a deleted site counts), it loses events:read or alerts:read, a manager disables the webhook, or the destination is no longer permitted. A receiver that keeps failing does not disable it. Saving the endpoint again turns it back on with a new secret, starting at the journal's head: history is not replayed.

boxes.label: Cancelled
boxes.detail: A delivery prepared for an earlier endpoint revision, or for a device that has left the grant, is never sent.

steps.text: An alert activates. The transaction that records it also appends alert.activated.v1 to the organization's journal, so the event exists exactly when the change does.
The webhooks worker passes over every enabled webhook about once a second. Nothing is scheduled on the path that evaluates telemetry.
If the application was revoked or its grant changed since the webhook was saved, the worker disables the webhook and cancels what is pending.
Otherwise it takes the next event for a granted device and stores a pending delivery with the body it will send.
Before sending, everything is checked again under a lock, so a revocation waits for a send in progress and stops every later one.
A delivery for an old endpoint revision or a device no longer granted is cancelled.
The destination is resolved and validated, then the body is signed with the webhook's secret.
The receiver gets the POST with the delivery ID, a timestamp and the signature. It verifies the signature over the raw body and drops IDs it has seen.
Any 2xx within 5 seconds marks the delivery delivered.
No answer, 408, 425, 429 or a 5xx puts it back to pending: the next tries come after 10 seconds, 30 seconds, 2 minutes and 10 minutes.
After five attempts or 24 hours, or on any other response, the delivery fails. The application catches up through the event feed.
A manager can retry a failed delivery in the portal, which gives it five more attempts.
